subject: PayGrid — Model fit eval & parity next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tharris@paygrid.com>, Priya Kumar <pkumar@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: PayGrid — Model fit eval & parity next steps

Hi Tom / Priya — great speaking with you earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Recap
- Main goal: replace/augment PayGrid's proprietary NLU baseline for payments routing & account reconciliation with an open-model stack that meets your quality bar while reducing unit cost.
- Primary evaluation axes: intent classification accuracy, downstream extraction exact-match, hallucination rate, latency (p99), and cost/TCO.

Recommended starting models to evaluate (fast path)
1) redwood/llama2-chat-13b (q4_k_m quantized) — best cost/quality balance for chat-like flows
2) redpajama-incite-3b-instruct (fp16) — lower-cost option for high-throughput rule-based prompts
3) redwood/llama2-70b (int4) — closer to your proprietary baseline on quality but higher cost; use only if parity target not met by 13B

Acceptance / parity suggestions (to make objective)
- Intent accuracy >= 90% (absolute) OR >= 0.95x relative to baseline on your labelled set
- Extraction exact-match >= 0.9x relative to baseline
- Hallucination rate <= baseline + 3 percentage points (measured via sample human review)
- Latency p95 <= 2x baseline for streaming endpoints (we expect lower for 13B; 70B may be higher)

What we need from you (short list)
- A 1,000–2,000 prompt sample set (we've attached paygrid_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) — can be a mix of labelled/unlabelled.
- If you have gold labels for intents/extractions, share paygrid_gold_labels_v1.csv so we can run labelled metrics; otherwise we can run a blind eval + human review.

What Redwood will do
- Run a 72-hour evaluation across the recommended model variants on Hosted/Dedicated (we can provision dedicated infra for parity runs).
- Produce benchmark report: per-model intent accuracy, extraction EM, ROUGE-L relative to baseline, hallucination flags, latency/cost per 1k tokens. Link will be published to the shared folder.
- Flag any quality regressions and recommend mitigation (prompt engineering, quantization profile changes, or larger model).

Links & artifacts
- Evaluation harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness
- Benchmark dashboard (placeholder — we'll publish results here): https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/paygrid-2026

Proposed next steps
1) You confirm the sample set and whether you can share gold labels (reply to this thread).
2) We schedule a kickoff with engineering (30–45m) for Tuesday 10/5 to align on metrics and dataset.
3) Redwood kicks off the 72-hour run and delivers results + a parity recommendation within 5 business days after completion.

Estimated cost for a dedicated parity run (3 days): ~$6,500 (one-time eval capacity) — we can provide an exact quote after kickoff.

If that plan looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff — otherwise tell me what to adjust.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications before we commit: 
1) On parity metrics: our internal baseline scores are ~94% intent accuracy and ~0.88 extraction EM on the 2k labelled set. When you say 0.95x relative, do you mean Redwood expects 0.95 * 94% = 89.3% as “acceptable”? That feels lower than we’d accept. What's your experience converting relative thresholds to business impact?
2) Hallucination: we care a lot about hallucination on financial entities (amounts, account IDs). Can you confirm how you measure hallucination at scale (we don't have bandwidth for full manual review)?
3) Cost: curious if the $6.5k estimate assumes dedicated infra or hosted. Can you break down the components?

We can share the prompt set today; labels are still finalizing — might be able to deliver ~1k labels by next Monday.

—Tom

Subject: Re: PayGrid — Model fit eval & parity next steps

Hi Tom — jumping in on the tech details. Short answers first, then specifics:

1) Parity framing: we typically propose a mix of absolute and relative thresholds. For enterprise buys, customers often require absolute floors (e.g., intent >= 92%) plus a relative parity check vs. their most important slices. Given your baseline (94%), a conservative acceptance would be intent >= 92% AND >= 0.98x baseline on high-priority intents. That reduces business risk vs. a purely relative threshold.

2) Hallucination measurement approach
- Automated filters: we run an entity-type detector on outputs (e.g., currency, account-id patterns) and flag mismatches vs. input context. This catches many obvious hallucinations.
- Sampled manual review: for financial entities we run a stratified sample (~200 cases) to surface edge hallucinations; human reviewers label hallucination/usability.
- Metric: hallucination rate = (# hallucinated cases in sample / sample size). We report both absolute and delta vs. baseline.

3) Cost breakdown for the 72-hour parity run
- Infra (GPU time on Dedicated) ~ $4,200
- Engineering setup & evaluation run ~ $1,300
- Human review (stratified sample) ~ $1,000
= Total ~= $6,500 (estimate). If you run on Hosted (shared) we can reduce infra cost but results may vary slightly for p95 latency; we’ll call that out.

Evaluation plan (technical)
- If you provide gold labels (paygrid_gold_labels_v1.csv) we will compute standard metrics (accuracy, EM, ROUGE-L) directly.
- If labels are partial/unavailable: we’ll run blind model-to-model comparisons and a human review on a stratified sample (entities + failure modes).
- We'll also produce per-intent and per-entity-slice charts so we can identify where open models fall short (e.g., low-frequency intents).

Attachments included in this email (attached for your review):
- paygrid_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (1k sample prompts)
- paygrid_gold_labels_v1.csv (if you can confirm these are final)
- paygrid_mutual_action_plan.pdf (proposed timeline & owners)

Let us know if you want us to prioritize hallucination checks over other slices — we can increase manual review budget on those slices.

Action items I can pick up once you confirm:
- Schedule dedicated 72-hour run (we reserve capacity).
- Prep the evaluation harness on your dataset and run the first pass with Llama2-13B (q4_k_m) + RedPajama-3B.
- Deliver the benchmark report and suggested mitigation options.

Thanks — happy to discuss on the kickoff.
